findings.title: Feature-flagged table visualization discards all dashboard query results
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the new `TableWidgetVisualization` is always given `columns={[]}` and a hard-coded empty `tableData` object instead of `result.data`, `result.meta`, and the widget fields. Consequently every table widget for organizations with this feature renders an empty table regardless of the query result, replacing the existing populated `StyledSimpleTableChart`.

findings.title: Browser report validation permits reports with neither timestamp nor age
findings.body: Both spec-specific fields are optional and validation only runs when one is supplied, so a report containing neither `timestamp` nor `age` is accepted and counted. The endpoint claims to support the two formats, each of which requires its respective timing field; accepting neither lets malformed reports pollute the collection metrics. Add object-level validation requiring exactly one of the two fields.

findings.title: Mutual exclusion of age and timestamp fails for zero values
findings.body: The checks use `self.initial_data.get(...)`, which treats `0` as absent. Thus a request with `timestamp: 0` and `age: 0` passes validation even though it mixes the two mutually exclusive reporting formats. Presence should be checked with key membership (or object-level validated data), not truthiness.

findings.title: Error IDs can be paired with the wrong nodestore event when an event is missing
findings.body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a mapping, but the implementation pairs `error_ids` with `events.values()` by position. If the backend omits a missing node from the mapping (as multi-get implementations commonly do), all subsequent values shift and error details are attributed to the wrong replay error IDs. Look up each result by its generated node ID and retain the corresponding original event ID rather than zipping with mapping values.

findings.title: Falsy custom cell render results incorrectly invoke the fallback renderer
findings.body: The documented renderer contract says fallback rendering occurs when a custom renderer returns `undefined`, but this code uses `if (cell)`. Intentional valid React render results such as `0`, an empty string, or `false` are treated as absent and replaced by the default field renderer. Test specifically for `cell !== undefined` (and make the same correction in the header renderer at line 31).
